title: U.S. House · Washington's 8th District
area: Central Washington suburbs and exurbs east of Seattle, including Issaquah, Sammamish, Wenatchee, and Ellensburg.

context.text: Washington uses a top-two primary open to all voters regardless of party. Incumbent Kim Schrier and Spencer Meline advanced from the August 4, 2026 primary over a crowded Republican field that included Trinh Ha, Bob Hagglund, and Andres Valleza, and Democrat Keith Arnold. Schrier won the primary with 53.8% of the vote.

summary.text: Kim Schrier is the Democratic incumbent for Washington's 8th Congressional District. A pediatrician who practiced in Issaquah, she was elected to Congress in 2018 and, according to her official biography, is the first pediatrician in Congress. She serves on the Energy and Commerce Committee and cites her work as a physician and her own type 1 diabetes in her health care focus.

background.text: According to her official biography, grew up the daughter of a public school teacher and an engineer.

Earned a bachelor's degree in astrophysics from the University of California, Berkeley in 1991 (graduating Phi Beta Kappa, per her official biography) and spent a year working at the Environmental Protection Agency before medical school.

Earned an M.D. from the University of California, Davis in 1997 and completed a pediatrics residency at Stanford University School of Medicine (her official biography names Lucile Packard Children's Hospital at Stanford).

Began working as a pediatrician in 2000 and spent her career before Congress as a pediatrician in Issaquah; her official biography says Parents Map Magazine named her Best Pediatrician in the Greater Seattle Area in 2013.
Has type 1 diabetes, diagnosed at age 16, which she cites in her work on healthcare and prescription drug costs.
Elected to Congress on November 6, 2018, and took office in January 2019; her official biography describes her as the first pediatrician in Congress.

In the 119th Congress, serves on the Energy and Commerce Committee (Health; Energy; and Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade subcommittees). Earlier terms included the Education and Labor and Agriculture Committees.
Her official site lists her as Chair of the Democratic Doctors Caucus and a Rural Revitalization Working Group chair within the New Democrat Coalition.
According to her official biography, lives in Sammamish with her husband and son.

priorities.text: Highlights healthcare affordability, gun safety, and the economy and trade as core campaign issues, drawing on her background as a pediatrician and patient.

positions.summary: Says she has worked on legislation to end surprise medical billing, prevent Medicare cuts and strengthen the ACA, and re-introduced a bill on children's access to pediatric care.
positions.quote: I have worked to get bills passed into law to end surprise medical billing, prevent Medicare cuts, and make healthcare more affordable by shoring up the ACA.

positions.summary: Says she will protect a woman's right to choose and keep politicians out of medical decisions between a woman and her doctor.
positions.quote: As a doctor, I will always fight to protect a woman's right to choose and to keep politicians out of private decisions between a woman and her doctor.

positions.summary: Supports background-check expansion and other gun-safety measures while saying she backs the rights of responsible gun owners; cosponsored universal background-check legislation and helped pass the bipartisan Safer Communities Act.
positions.quote: I cosponsored universal, comprehensive background check legislation in Congress because guns should never be allowed in the hands of someone with a history of domestic violence, a violent criminal record, convicted stalkers, or those with severe mental illness.

positions.summary: Says climate change requires immediate action, cosponsored the Climate Action Now Act to keep the U.S. in the Paris Climate Accords, and supports action to reduce carbon emissions and create clean energy jobs.
positions.quote: Climate change is real and I know we must take immediate action.

positions.summary: Says she will make the wealthiest corporations pay their fair share of taxes without raising taxes on middle-class families.
positions.quote: I will bring financial relief to families experiencing these rising costs by finally making sure the wealthiest corporations pay their fair share of taxes, without raising taxes on middle-class families.

positions.summary: Says she sponsored a bill to triple funding for COPS grants and voted to increase law enforcement funding, and says she opposes efforts to defund the police.
positions.quote: I sponsored the COPS on the Beat Grant Program Reauthorization and Parity Act that would triple funding for COPS grants

record.text: Re-introduced the Helping Families Access Pediatric Care Act (H.R. 8573) to expand access to pediatric care.
Sponsored a bill, signed into law, to speed federal approval of generic insulin to bring down costs.
Cosponsored the reauthorization of the Violence Against Women Act, which includes provisions to keep guns from people convicted of domestic-violence offenses.

summary.text: Spencer Meline is the Republican nominee for Washington's 8th Congressional District. He describes himself as a small business owner and father of four, born and raised in Edmonds and now living in Cashmere. He describes himself as not a career politician and is running on lowering the cost of living, supporting small businesses and public-lands stewardship.

background.text: Born and raised in Edmonds, Washington; now lives in Cashmere in the 8th District.

Built businesses from the ground up in Leavenworth, Washington, gaining experience managing payroll, navigating regulations, and leading teams; Ballotpedia lists his career experience as business owner.
Describes himself as husband and father of four; he and his wife homeschool their children, and he says faith is central to his family.
According to his campaign website, has spent years hiking, climbing and fishing in the 8th District and describes himself as "not a career politician."
His campaign website lists the Washington State Republican Party as an endorser.
Advanced from the August 4, 2026 top-two primary, finishing second with 15.9% of the vote behind Schrier.

priorities.text: Lists strong small businesses, lowering the cost of living, safe communities, responsible stewardship of public lands, and smart and secure immigration as his campaign's priorities.

Says small businesses are the backbone of the district's economy and that his own experience building businesses gives him a practical understanding of how federal policy affects employers and workers.
priorities.quote: Small businesses are the backbone of Washington's 8th District. When small businesses are strong, communities are strong, workers have opportunity, and the American Dream is within reach.

statements.quote: Public safety starts with supporting well-trained and properly funded law enforcement.
statements.context: On his campaign website (July 16, 2026), as quoted by Ballotpedia

statements.quote: We need a secure border so we can stop trafficking and cartel activity and enforce immigration law consistently.
statements.context: On his campaign website (July 16, 2026), as quoted by Ballotpedia

statements.quote: Encourage housing construction by reducing unnecessary regulatory barriers and using federal infrastructure and housing programs in ways that increase supply while respecting state and local authority over land use.
statements.context: On his campaign website's priorities page

statements.quote: America should pursue abundant, reliable energy, including hydropower, nuclear power, renewables, natural gas, and domestic oil production, to strengthen energy security and keep utility and transportation costs manageable.
statements.context: On his campaign website's priorities page

researchNotes: Schrier's healthcare and gun-safety statements are drawn from active issue pages on her campaign website; other issue subpages (economy/trade) returned no fetchable content. Meline completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his fuller responses were not exhaustively transcribed given the basic research tier. Schrier's federal key votes and FEC totals are added separately by script. Meline's issue statements are drawn from his campaign priorities page and the website text Ballotpedia quotes in his Candidate Connection entry; he takes no stance on the guide's issue statements in a form that could be recorded as a position. Meline's campaign website and Ballotpedia survey do not list schooling or past employers beyond his own businesses, and no news profile was found.
